fact_checks: The verified fact confirms that applicationinterface.protocol is a required string enum listing HTTP and HTTPS as separate values alongside gRPC, AMQP, WebSocket, REST, GraphQL and SOAP.

The current schema's attribute description says to use application-level protocols only and that network/transport-level protocols such as TLS belong in the Technology Layer; the verified fact truncates this text but does not contradict it.
The verified facts show 'protocol' is declared on exactly one type in the application layer, so a merge would affect only applicationinterface.protocol.
The enum also mixes REST, an architectural style over HTTP, with HTTP itself, so the value list does not strictly keep to a single abstraction level beyond the HTTP/HTTPS split.

arguments_for: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS. A separate value encodes the very transport concern the attribute's own description assigns to the Technology Layer.
The contradiction is internal to one attribute: the enum and its description disagree. A modeller following the guidance cannot tell which to obey.
Only one type declares protocol, so merging the two values is a contained, low-blast-radius correction.
arguments_against: Merging is a breaking enum change. Existing models that use HTTPS would fail validation unless they are migrated.
Leaving HTTPS in the enum harms nothing functionally. A tightened description might resolve the tension without removing the value.
The enum already mixes abstraction levels, such as REST alongside HTTP, so a strict purity standard is not clearly the spec's intent.

arguments_for: HTTPS is a distinct URI scheme that is commonly treated as an application-level protocol name. Modellers and extractors reading 'https://' endpoints get a direct mapping.
The guidance may be meant to exclude raw TCP/TLS entries, not to forbid a recognised scheme name like HTTPS.
arguments_against: The description explicitly names TLS as belonging to the Technology Layer, and HTTPS differs from HTTP only by TLS.
Nothing in the layer intent or the definition justifies encoding transport security on an application interface.

arguments_for: Whether HTTPS counts as a protocol name or as a transport detail is debatable. Practitioners commonly treat it either way.
Fixing this could mean merging the values or rewording the guidance. Choosing between them is a product decision about the enum's granularity.
Migration cost for existing HTTPS models has to be weighed against conceptual purity.
arguments_against: The attribute's own text already makes the call, naming TLS as a Technology Layer concern, so little is left to decide.
Keeping both values leaves the documented contradiction in place whichever way the product leans.

arguments_for: One could argue that TLS handling is a Technology or Security layer matter rather than the application layer's.
arguments_against: The claim concerns the application layer's own enum values, which the spec explicitly defines and models.
The claim is about the spec's schema, not about tooling or the CLI.
